literal: He piled up leave-slips in straw sandals to murder the emperor, and rode mist-veiled robes toward heaven.
idiomatic: Piling up leave-slips in straw sandals, he murdered the emperor; riding robe-mist, he claimed heaven.

literal: He brought swift disaster in the fourth month—how could one hear of the Way's ten years?
idiomatic: Swift disaster in the fourth month—what of the Way's ten-year promise?

literal: (After Terrace City fell, Emperor Wu of Liang once sat alone and sighed: "In wen Hou Jing is a petty man's hundred-day Son of Heaven.
idiomatic: (After Terrace City fell, Emperor Wu of Liang sat alone and sighed: "In wen, Hou Jing is a petty man's hundred-day Son of Heaven.

literal: " When Jing illegally took the throne on the nineteenth day of the eleventh month in the second year of Dabao, until the nineteenth day of the third month the next year he abandoned the city and fled—a hundred and twenty days; by the Way of Heaven's reckoning of great numbers, in wen it is "a hundred days."
idiomatic: " When Jing usurped the throne on the nineteenth of the eleventh month, year two of Dabao, and on the nineteenth of the third month the next year abandoned the city and fled, it was a hundred and twenty days; by Heaven's great reckoning, in wen that reads as a hundred days.

literal: " The words, like Gongsun Shu's, both receive twelve—yet ten-day years differ.)
idiomatic: " The phrase, like Gongsun Shu's, shares twelve—yet the ten-day count differs.)

literal: Taken captive by Di barbarians on the old soil, sunk in barbarian ways on the homeward turn.
idiomatic: Taken captive by Di on native soil, sunk in barbarian custom on the road home.

literal: Grieving "Pleasant Valley" in the clear temple, mourning "Wheat in Ear" in empty market stalls.
idiomatic: He grieved "Pleasant Valley" in the clear temple, mourned "Wheat in Ear" in empty stalls.

literal: Toy drums lie unstruck; the great bell is shattered and no longer hung.
idiomatic: Toy drums lie unplayed; the great bell lies broken, unhung.

literal: Wilds desolate with bones strewn across them; towns silent, without smoke.
idiomatic: The wilds were desolate, bones strewn across them; towns stood silent, without smoke.

literal: Of the hundred clans, perhaps some still exist,
idiomatic: Of the hundred clans, perhaps some still survived,

literal: (A hundred families of Central Plains gentry who crossed the Yangzi with the Jin—hence Jiangdong had the Hundred Genealogies; those in the capital were almost entirely destroyed.)
idiomatic: (A hundred families of Central Plains gentry who crossed the Yangzi with Jin—hence Jiangdong kept the Hundred Genealogies; those still in the capital were nearly all destroyed.)

literal: five generations overthrown and cut down.
idiomatic: five generations were overthrown and cut down.

literal: Only Princess Zhaojun's lament was played; only Princess Wengzhu's mournful strings.
idiomatic: Only Princess Zhaojun's lament sounded; only Princess Wengzhu's grieving strings.

literal: (The princesses' sons and daughters were shamed and killed.)
idiomatic: (The princesses' sons and daughters were shamed and slain.)

literal: Passing Changgan in suppressed grief,
idiomatic: He passed Changgan in suppressed grief,

literal: (Changgan was the old Yan family lane.)
idiomatic: (Changgan was the old lane of the Yan house.)

literal: unfolding through Baixia in lingering sorrow.
idiomatic: and lingered through Baixia in sorrow that would not leave.

literal: (Seven generations of tombs from Jing Marquis downward all lay at Baixia.)
idiomatic: (Seven generations of tombs from Jing Marquis down all lay at Baixia.)

literal: Deeply feeling what swallows and sparrows recall, moved by native earth's old devotion.
idiomatic: He felt deeply what swallows and sparrows remember, and was moved by the old devotion of native earth.

literal: He found this heart in Confucius; he trusted these words of Wang Can.
idiomatic: In Confucius he found this heart; in Wang Can he trusted these words.

literal: From afar the western lands had multitudes; he relied on Fang Shu for the light campaign.
idiomatic: From afar the western lands had hosts; he leaned on Fang Shu for a light punitive strike.

literal: (The Duke of Yongning, as Minister over the Masses, was Grand Commander.)
idiomatic: (The Duke of Yongning served as Minister over the Masses and Grand Commander.)

literal: He stroked ringing swords with thunder's roar and shook heroic banners like scudding clouds.
idiomatic: He stroked ringing swords till thunder roared, shook heroic banners till clouds scudded.

literal: A thousand li he chased their flight; three years he exhausted their nests and dens.
idiomatic: A thousand li he chased their flight; three years he wore out their nests and dens.

literal: He slew Chiyou in the eastern commandery and hung Zhizhi's head on the northern gate.
idiomatic: He slew Chiyou in the eastern commandery and hung Zhizhi's head on the northern gate.

literal: (After beheading Hou Jing, they boiled the corpse in the Jiankang market; the people ate until the flesh was gone and gnawed the bones; the head was sent to Jingzhou and hung on the capital street.
idiomatic: (After Hou Jing was beheaded, his corpse was boiled in the Jiankang market; commoners ate until the flesh was gone and gnawed the bones; the head was sent to Jingzhou and hung on the capital street.

literal: He mourned wronged souls in the dark, swept overgrown imperial mounds.
idiomatic: He mourned wronged shades, swept imperial mounds choked with weeds.

literal: Thus the Yin way was revived; Xia sacrifices were not neglected thereby.
idiomatic: Thus the Yin way rose again; Xia sacrifices were not neglected.

literal: But regret remained for Flame-Kun: fire spread through the palace for months on end.
idiomatic: But regret lingered for Flame-Kun—fire ran through the palace for months.

literal: (After Hou Jing fled, the loyalist army, gathering rudders, accidentally set fire and burned the palaces utterly.)
idiomatic: (After Hou Jing fled, the loyalist army, gathering rudders, lost control of fire and burned the palaces to nothing.)

literal: I pointed my oars toward the two easts and attended the five deferrals on the ascending altar.
idiomatic: I pointed my oars toward the two easts and attended the five deferrals at the ascending altar.

literal: I rejoiced to see Han officials again and answered the Chu people's hopes.
idiomatic: I rejoiced to see Han officials again and answered what the Chu people had hoped for.

literal: Wearing crimson robes I presented memorials, humbly holding Yellow Gate duties amid office slander.
idiomatic: In crimson robes I presented memorials, humbly bearing Yellow Gate office amid slander.

literal: (At the time he was Irregular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, presenting affairs of the lodge.)
idiomatic: (At the time he was irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry, presenting lodge affairs.)

literal: Sometimes he collated Stone Canal texts,
idiomatic: Sometimes he collated Stone Canal texts,

literal: (Minister Wang memorialized sending eighty thousand juan of secret-repository old records; an edict ordered comparison and collation, divided into principal, secondary, and miscellaneous sets.
idiomatic: (Minister Wang memorialized sending eighty thousand juan of secret-repository records; an edict ordered collation into principal, secondary, and miscellaneous sets.

literal: Zhou Hongzheng, Minister of the Left for the People, Peng Senglang, gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Wang Gui and Dai Ling, direct-province scholars, collated the Classics section; Wang Bao, Left Vice Director, Zong Huaizheng, Minister of Personnel, Yan Zhitui, irregular gentleman, Liu Renying, direct scholar, collated History; Yin Buhai, Director of Justice, Wang Xiaoji, censor-in-chief, Deng Shen, secretariat gentleman, Xu Bao, director of the Gold Bureau, collated Masters; Yu Xin, General of the Right Guard, Wang Gu, literary aide to Prince of Jin'an, Zong Shanye, Zhou Que, direct scholars, collated Collectanea.)
idiomatic: Zhou Hongzheng of the Left for the People, Peng Senglang of the Yellow Gate, Wang Gui and Dai Ling of the direct province collated Classics; Wang Bao, Left Vice Director, Zong Huaizheng of Personnel, Yan Zhitui as irregular gentleman, Liu Renying as direct scholar collated History; Yin Buhai of Justice, censor-in-chief Wang Xiaoji, Deng Shen of the Secretariat, Xu Bao of the Gold Bureau collated Masters; Yu Xin of the Right Guard, Wang Gu, Zong Shanye of Jin'an, Zhou Que collated Collectanea.)

literal: at times joining the Bo Liang hymns.
idiomatic: at times joining the Bo Liang hymns.

literal: He regarded jars and caldrons as beyond counting and washed in waves without measure.
idiomatic: He looked on jars and caldrons as beyond count and bathed in waves without measure.

literal: When Xiangyang bore guilt,
idiomatic: When Xiangyang bore guilt,

literal: (Lu Na.)
idiomatic: (Lu Na.)

literal: and Min-Emei proclaimed itself king,
idiomatic: and Min-Emei made itself king,

literal: (the Prince of Wuling.)
idiomatic: (the Prince of Wuling.)

literal: he waited till things were settled to ring the phoenix carriage and restore the Eastern Capital's great magnificence.
idiomatic: he waited till order returned to ring the phoenix carriage and rebuild the Eastern Capital's grandeur.

literal: (An edict ordered Minister of Agriculture Huang Chao to build the halls.)
idiomatic: (An edict ordered Minister of Agriculture Huang Chao to build the halls.)

literal: Startled that the north wind rose again, grieved that southern songs would not flow.
idiomatic: He was startled when the north wind rose again, grieved when southern songs would not flow.

literal: (Qin troops came in succession.)
idiomatic: (Qin troops came again and again.)

literal: He held the golden city's boiling moat and turned the crimson palace's jade canopy.
idiomatic: He held the golden city's boiling moat and turned the crimson palace's jade canopy.

literal: (Emperor Xiaoyuan understood yin-yang and military arts; when he first heard rebels were coming he used much exorcism; after the siege, he sighed repeatedly, knowing defeat was certain.)
idiomatic: (Emperor Xiaoyuan knew yin-yang and military arts; when rebels first came he relied on exorcism; under siege he sighed again and again, knowing he must fall.)

literal: He had the Way and his army was upright—yet reversed, without a righteous name he could not resist.
idiomatic: He had the Way and a straight army—yet without a righteous name he could not hold out.

literal: (Xiaoyuan and Chancellor Yuwen pledged like severed metal; soon he was destroyed—an army without righteous name.)
idiomatic: (Xiaoyuan and Chancellor Yuwen pledged like severed metal; soon he was destroyed—the campaign had no righteous name.)

literal: A million people became captives; a thousand cartloads of books went up in smoke and ash.
idiomatic: A million people were taken captive; a thousand cartloads of books burned to ash.

literal: Under the broad heaven, all culture perished.
idiomatic: Under broad heaven, all culture perished.

literal: (In the north, tomb records were less than a third of Jiangdong's; Liang's stripping and chaos scattered and drowned them.
idiomatic: (In the north, tomb records were less than a third of Jiangdong's; Liang's stripping and chaos scattered and drowned them.

literal: Only Xiaoyuan gathered them, more than a hundred thousand in all—unprecedented in historical records.
idiomatic: Only Xiaoyuan gathered them—more than a hundred thousand in all—unprecedented in the records.

literal: Defeat burned them all; within the seas there were no book houses again.)
idiomatic: Defeat burned them all; within the seas there were no book houses again.)

literal: He pitied infants and children—what was their crime? He grieved for the old and sick—without proper form.
idiomatic: He pitied infants—what crime had they? He grieved for the old and sick left without proper burial.

literal: Seized from arms and abandoned to the grass, they stumbled on the roads and suffered plunder.
idiomatic: Torn from arms and cast on the grass, they fell on the roads and were plundered.

literal: He resented cruelty to the imperial carriage and grieved the lawless state of man and spirits.
idiomatic: He resented cruelty to the imperial carriage and grieved that man and spirits had lost all law.

literal: He mounted the cart of dismissal for mourning and covered the rush-and-tung coffin's sparse burial.
idiomatic: He rode the cart of dismissal in mourning and covered the rush-and-tung coffin's sparse burial.

literal: Clouds without heart drifted along; wind harbored rage and restlessness.
idiomatic: Clouds drifted without heart; wind nursed rage and would not rest.

literal: Jing Bo drank ox in the Qin region; Ziqing herded sheep by the sea.
idiomatic: Jing Bo drank with his ox in Qin; Ziqing herded sheep by the sea.

literal: The sword-belt wife—people mourned her severance;
idiomatic: The sword-belt wife—people mourned her severance;

literal: the stone-chime player's son—families wound themselves in grief.
idiomatic: the stone-chime player's son—households wrapped themselves in grief.

literal: This petty minister shamed to die alone, truly ashamed before barbarian faces, leading lame foot toward the road,
idiomatic: This petty minister shamed to die alone, ashamed before barbarian faces, dragging lame foot toward the road,

literal: (at the time suffering from foot qi.)
idiomatic: (at the time he suffered from foot qi.)

literal: driving a lame nag into the pass.
idiomatic: driving a lame nag into the pass.

literal: (Post horses exhausted, donkeys and horses thin.)
idiomatic: (Post horses were exhausted; donkeys and horses were thin.)

literal: Below, no shadow yet he must tread; above, a span yet he must climb quickly.
idiomatic: Below there was no shadow yet he had to tread on; above, a span yet he had to climb fast.

literal: Alas—the flying tumbleweed's days are long; hatred—the drifting stem never returns.
idiomatic: Alas—the flying tumbleweed's days stretch on; hatred—the drifting stem never comes home.

literal: As for black-ox banners, nine-dragon roads, earth gui measuring shadow, armillary sphere verifying degrees—
idiomatic: As for black-ox banners, nine-dragon roads, the earth gui measuring shadow, the armillary sphere fixing degrees—

literal: sometimes former sages' models, sometimes former kings' statutes.
idiomatic: sometimes a former sage's model, sometimes a former king's statute.

literal: They perished together with the divine tripod; one cuts off the immortal palace forever missed.
idiomatic: They sank with the divine tripod; the immortal palace was cut off forever, only missed.

literal: Then the sixteen kingdoms' customs, seventy generations' commanderies—heard and seen but unreachable; sung in maps and books, only imaginable.
idiomatic: The sixteen kingdoms' customs, seventy generations' commanderies—heard and seen but unreachable; sung in maps and books, only imaginable.

literal: Why are the black-haired folk not as of old? Only mountains and rivers remain as before.
idiomatic: Why are the people not as they were? Only mountains and rivers stay as before.

literal: Each time he knotted thoughts on rivers and lakes, about to take harm from nets.
idiomatic: Each time he knotted his thoughts on rivers and lakes, about to be taken in nets.

literal: He heard bamboo of another age's grief and listened to the frontier song's clear cry.
idiomatic: He heard another age's bamboo grief and listened to the frontier song's clear cry.

literal: Facing the bright moon, sorrow grew; before the fragrant cup, no delight.
idiomatic: Facing the bright moon, sorrow grew; before the fragrant cup, there was no delight.

literal: From strife within Great Clarity, they from Heavenly Qi invaded from without.
idiomatic: From strife within Great Clarity, Heavenly Qi invaded from without.

literal: First they cramped the state at the Huai shore; then pressed the border at the Yangzi bank.
idiomatic: First they cramped the state at the Huai shore; then pressed the border at the Yangzi bank.

literal: (In Hou Jing's rebellion, Qi deeply stripped Liang's territory; north and south of the Huai only Lujiang, Jinxi, Gaotang, Xincai, Xiyang, and Qichang commanderies remained.
idiomatic: (In Hou Jing's rebellion, Qi deeply stripped Liang's territory; north and south of the Huai only Lujiang, Jinxi, Gaotang, Xincai, Xiyang, and Qichang remained.

literal: At Xiaoyuan's defeat, then all was gone—the Yangzi became the border.)
idiomatic: At Xiaoyuan's defeat, all was gone—the Yangzi became the border.)

literal: They gained benevolent and thick horn of qilin and overcame outstanding southern gold.
idiomatic: They gained the qilin's benevolent horn and overcame outstanding southern gold.

literal: They gathered hosts and installed a ruler; five hundred chariots came from afar,
idiomatic: They gathered hosts and installed a ruler; five hundred chariots came from afar,

literal: (Qi sent Prince of Shangdang Huan leading tens of thousands to install Liang's Marquis of Zhenyang Ming as ruler.)
idiomatic: (Qi sent Prince of Shangdang Huan with tens of thousands to install Liang's Marquis of Zhenyang Ming as ruler.)

literal: They returned Jizi's viewing of music and released Zhong Yi's drum and zither.
idiomatic: They returned Jizi to his music and released Zhong Yi from drum and zither.

literal: (Liang's envoys Xie Ting and Xu Ling at last could return south; all Liang subjects were sent off with ceremony.)
idiomatic: (Liang's envoys Xie Ting and Xu Ling at last returned south; all Liang subjects were sent off with ceremony.)

literal: Secretly hearing the wind, ears grew clear; leaning toward the seen sun, hearts turned homeward.
idiomatic: Hearing the wind in secret, ears grew clear; leaning toward the seen sun, hearts turned homeward.

literal: He tried brushing the yarrow for a true divination and met Mount Tai's auspicious fortune in the hexagram.
idiomatic: He brushed the yarrow for a true divination and met auspicious fortune in the hexagram of Tai.

literal: (Zhitui heard Liang people were returning to the state and therefore had a mind to flee to Qi.
idiomatic: (Zhitui heard Liang people were returning home and therefore meant to flee to Qi.

literal: On New Year's day of the bingzi year he divined whether going east was auspicious and met Tai changing to Kan; he rejoiced and said: "Heaven and earth join in Tai and turn to practice; Kan doubles peril, yet going without losing faith—this is an auspicious hexagram, only I regret small going and great coming."
idiomatic: On New Year's day of the bingzi year he divined whether going east was auspicious and met Tai changing to Kan; he rejoiced and said, "Heaven and earth join in Tai and turn to practice; Kan doubles peril, yet the journey keeps faith—an auspicious hexagram, only I regret small going and great coming."

literal: " Later it indeed proved auspicious.)
idiomatic: " Later it indeed proved auspicious.)

literal: It was like wishing for Qin yet changing to Chu, borrowing the southern road toward eastern Xun.
idiomatic: It was like wishing for Qin yet changing to Chu, borrowing the southern road toward eastern Xun.

literal: He rode one bend of Dragon Gate and passed the twin peaks of Dizhu.
idiomatic: He rode one bend of Dragon Gate and passed the twin peaks of Dizhu.

literal: Ice Spirit thinned the wind and thunder roared; Yang Lord bore mountains and valleys sank.
idiomatic: Ice Spirit thinned the wind and thunder roared; Yang Lord bore mountains and valleys sank.

literal: He matched one who carried the turtle to ford the deep and was like one who slew the flood dragon and plunged into the depths.
idiomatic: He matched one who carried the turtle to ford the deep and was like one who slew the flood dragon and plunged into the depths.

literal: At dusk he raised sails at Fen-Shan; at dawn he moored at Heyin.
idiomatic: At dusk he raised sails at Fen-Shan; at dawn he moored at Heyin.

literal: (Seven hundred li by water—they arrived in one night.)
idiomatic: (Seven hundred li by water—they arrived in one night.)

literal: He chased the swift wind's fleeing breath and followed loyalty and faith in his traveling song.
idiomatic: He chased the swift wind's fleeing breath and followed loyalty and faith in his traveling song.
